<jats:p>
                    The integration of zooarchaeological and palaeoenvironmental studies enables the evaluation of species distribution and abundance patterns in relation to climatic and environmental fluctuations through time. This study analyses rodent composition from modern Barn owl pellets (MNI = 138) and archaeological samples (MNI = 58) from the Casa de Piedra de Roselló (CP) archaeological locality (Central Patagonia), with the aim of assessing possible changes in species representation between the Late-Holocene and the present day. CP is located within the forest-steppe ecotone and features a long occupation sequence, ranging from ca. 9000 cal BP to historical times. For the final stages of the Holocene, the species
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Abrothrix hirta</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">A</jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">olivacea</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Ctenomys</jats:italic>
                    sp.,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Euneomys chinchilloides</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Geoxus</jats:italic>
                    sp.,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Loxodontomys micropus</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Microcavia australis</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Paynomys macronyx</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Reithrodon auritus</jats:italic>
                    were recorded. Except for
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">E</jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">chinchilloides</jats:italic>
                    , these species are characteristic of ecotonal forest-steppe environments.
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">E</jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">chinchilloides</jats:italic>
                    remained the dominant species while
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">A</jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">olivacea</jats:italic>
                    increased at present and forest-associated taxa such as
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Geoxus sp</jats:italic>
                    ., and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                    .
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">macronyx</jats:italic>
                    decreased or disappeared. The proportion of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Reithrodon auritus</jats:italic>
                    was also significantly higher in the archaeological sample compared with the current sample.
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Eligmodontia</jats:italic>
                    sp.,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Oligoryzomys longicaudatus</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Phyllotis xanthopygus</jats:italic>
                    are exclusive from the modern sample. Rather than reflecting a major environmental transformation, both rodents’ assemblages point to a predominantly semi-arid and open landscape, characterized by a substantial proportion of bare ground. At a finer micro-environmental scale, these changes in species composition suggest environmental shifts, from greater availability and extension of turf (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">mallin</jats:italic>
                    ) and grassy steppes in the final Late-Holocene to increased shrub expansion in recent times. Changes may be likely linked to post-Hispanic extensive livestock farming and overgrazing in the area.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《阿根廷丘布特省西南部罗塞略石屋考古遗址晚全新世小型哺乳动物及其古环境意义》：研究通过分析该遗址现代仓鸮食团与考古样本中的啮齿动物组成，探讨晚全新世至今物种构成的变化及其古环境指示意义，认为两组组合均指向以半干旱开阔景观为主的环境，物种组成变化可能反映从草甸和草类草原扩展到近期灌木扩张的微环境转变，值得关注。
items.title: Small mammals from the Late-Holocene of the archaeological locality Casa de Piedra de Roselló (southwest Chubut Province Argentina) and their paleoenvironmental implications

items.abstract: Integrated carbon isotope chemostratigraphy and palynological investigations from the Cretaceous-Paleogene vertebrate-bearing series of the Oudiksou Basin, Middle Atlas of Morocco Amelieh, Abdessamad; Oukassou, Mostafa; Yans, Johan; Hssaida, Touria; Khaffou, Hanane; Zafaty, Omar; Guinot, Guillaume; Mhamdi, Hicham Si; Charrière, André; Tabuce, Rodolphe Newsletters on Stratigraphy, (2026), p. - Abstract This study presents an integrated carbon isotope chemostratigraphy and palynological analysis of the Cretaceous–Paleogene vertebrate-bearing succession from the Oudiksou Basin in the Central Middle Atlas of Morocco. The studied sedimentary series preserves one of the rare terrestrial K–Pg records in North Africa. In addition to the previously documented paleontological data from Maastrichtian marine and continental sediments (elasmobranchs, charophytes, ostracods, and dinosaurs), our palynological investigations reveal additional dinoflagellate cyst data, leading to a better refinement of the biostratigraphic framework. Organic carbon isotope (δ13Corg) curves obtained from two lithostratigraphic sections across the Oudiksou basin reveal significant long-term trends that correlate confidently with global reference records. The Mid-Maastrichtian Event (MME ~ 68 Ma) is recorded in both marine and terrestrial settings, whereas the Late Danian Event (LDE ~ 62 Ma) is tentatively identified within strictly terrestrial environments. These isotopic events represent the first evidence of late Maastrichtian and early Paleogene paleoenvironmental and climatic changes documented in North Africa within this particular sedimentary context, characterized by a complex transition from marine to continental environments during the Cretaceous-Paleogene transition.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) is increasingly used in geoarchaeology because it enables rapid elemental measurements directly in the field or with minimal sample preparation. However, quantitative interpretation of pXRF data from unconsolidated sediments is complicated by matrix effects, moisture, grain-size heterogeneity, spectral interference, and the weak detection of light elements. We investigated these limitations using sediment samples from the Orkhon River Valley and Tsagaan Agui Cave in Mongolia. Samples were analyzed by an Olympus Vanta M-series pXRF analyzer and by an ARL 9900 XP laboratory wavelength-dispersive XRF spectrometer after fusion-bead preparation. The laboratory results were used as a reference dataset, and empirical regression equations were established for selected elements. The agreement between the two methods was element- and site-dependent. In the Orkhon River Valley, the strongest relationships were obtained for Fe and Ca, whereas Ti showed the weakest relationship. In the Tsagaan Agui Cave samples, Ca, Fe, and Mn showed the highest explanatory power, while Al showed the weakest relationship. These results indicate that pXRF data can rapidly reproduce major stratigraphic compositional trends under field-oriented conditions, but universal conversion equations should not be applied to different sedimentary or archaeological settings. In particular, Mg, Al, and Si may be underestimated in moist or heterogeneous sediments, and Na cannot generally be quantified reliably under standard air-path conditions. We recommend using pXRF primarily as a rapid field-screening tool for identifying compositional anomalies and stratigraphic intervals that require closer inspection, targeted sampling, or subsequent laboratory analysis. Where quantitative interpretation is required, pXRF data should be supported by matrix-matched calibration and laboratory validation.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Skeletal remains dating to 11,000 BP, excavated from the Qingshuiyuan Dadong site in Guizhou, are the earliest directly dated Early Holocene remains in southwestern China. This study applies carbon and nitrogen stable isotope analysis to the first molar dentin and rib samples from the relevant burial, revealing a diet primarily composed of C
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    foods and suggesting the preponderance of a freshwater fish diet. Dentin serial sampling revealed a late weaning, completed at approximately 2.75 years of age. This study of subsistence strategies and infant care practices of an Early Holocene individual in Guizhou, southwest China provides new evidence for depicting the lifeways of Holocene hunter‐gatherers in this area.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《想想孩子们：中国西南清水园洞穴遗址早全新世个体饮食研究》：该研究对贵州清水园大洞遗址距今约1.1万年的最早直接测年早全新世骨骼遗存，取第一磨牙牙本质与肋骨样品做碳氮稳定同位素分析，揭示其饮食以C3类食物为主并可能大量食用淡水鱼，牙本质序列取样还显示约2.75岁完成较晚断奶，为认识该地区全新世狩猎采集者的生计与婴儿照料提供了新证据。
items.title: Think of the Children: Early Holocene Individual Diet at the Qingshuiyuan Cave Site, Southwest China
